probe_result: A precommitted deadline plus post-deadline enumeration does not close the predecessor against late proposals. The decisive counterexample is a writer that passes an admission check before the boundary but makes its conflicting proposal durable only after the closer has authorized an effect. Claimed timestamps do not repair this unless admission is enforced by a non-forgeable transport/server fence. Therefore the bounded admission barrier is not a zero-dependency proof under the tested Chat-native role-local semantics.
mechanism_revision: Closure must be causal, not merely temporal. Either an admission primitive must durably fence all future predecessor-bound proposals before authorization, or the predecessor must avoid open competition by precommitting exactly one successor effect_id/payload_hash so every later materializer can only reproduce the same immutable effect.
scope_guard: Negative evidence is limited to one predecessor e2, two candidate writers, one locally checked precommitted boundary, immutable role-local proposal files, post-boundary enumeration, and one irreversible authorization point. It does not prove impossibility when a trusted server-enforced append cutoff, fencing token, linearizable CAS, predetermined closed membership with payload precommit, or equivalent admission primitive is available.
